additional_info.subject: RE: ID0371575-DC/SI-D /AE-[ MP / R5 170001908 ] Connectorld 2 error code CRM:00643000836
additional_info.body:
Hi Sadek,
Trust all is well!
Regarding the ticket, I have analyzed the logs for the day mentioned in the email trail from ticket creation. It appears that the electric vehicle (EV) being used by the customer/CPO was often at 100% State of Charge (SOC). In several instances where faults occurred at the outlets, these were due to cable disconnections. Specifically, when the DC pilot state was at B2, the cable was disconnected as the DC pilot state changed to A.
I suggest allowing some time between attempts to perform a charging session. Currently, the charger is functioning correctly with no error flags, and the charger’s health is normal. There is also an ongoing charging session on Outlet2.
Please conduct a few transactions with EVs that have a low SOC. If you encounter any issues, we are happy to assist and support you.
Regarding your previous queries:
The two earlier tickets addressed temperature-related issues, where there were either loose or no connections to BT sensors.
As for data consumption and log fetching via SIM cards, both routers send logs to the server. From there, we retrieve the logs, i.e., AWS for XF3 in SCB.
I hope this addresses your concerns. If there are no further topics to discuss, I recommend proceeding with closing this ticket.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shrey

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0371575-DC/SI-D /AE-[ MP / R5 170001908 ] Connectorld 2 error code CRM:00643000836
additional_info.body:
Hi Sadek,
I hope this email finds you well.
Regarding your issue, I discussed it with the experts, and we concluded that at 21:58 PM UTC, there was a successful charging session with the transaction ID: 285360881. After the car was successfully charged to 100% SOC, the cable was not disconnected, and multiple charging sessions were attempted during this time. There is no issue from the charger side. From the EV side, the contactors were toggling between ON/OFF because the cable remained connected while the EV was fully charged.
We have recently troubleshoot the charger, and there was also couple of successful charging session on Outlet 2. The previous two tickets were related to completely different issues(BT sensor), though the charger was the same.
I'm attaching the logs for your reference.
I hope you are satisfied with the answer provided. If so, shall we proceed with closing this ticket?
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shrey
